title: Cloud Connectors, Cloud Connector groups and Branch Connector groups under Private Access > Private Infrastructure

prose.label: Branch Connector groups.
prose.text: {{branch-connector-groups}} {{branch-connector-groups-page}} How a Cloud Connector group comes to exist differs between pages {{divergence:cloud-group-creation}}. The pages give no limits or group sizes, and do not say what the details drawers show {{gap:group-limits-and-drawers}}. The product itself is in [[cloud-connector.overview]], and the policy criterion that lists Branch Connector Groups is in [[zpa.policy.criteria]].

cloud-connector-what.statement: Cloud Connectors are VMs that simplify traffic forwarding to Zscaler services (Internet & SaaS and Private Access) and secure server access to the internet.

quotes: Cloud Connectors are virtual machines (VMs) that simplify traffic forwarding to Zscaler services (i.e., Internet & SaaS (ZIA) and Private Access (ZPA)).
The Cloud Connector also secures server access to the internet and provides direct connectivity to the Zscaler cloud

cloud-connector-benefits.statement: Cloud Connectors extend Internet & SaaS and Private Access capabilities to cloud-native workloads, simplify multi-cloud networking, and secure workload traffic to the internet while connecting to private applications in other cloud regions or data centers.

quotes: Extend the capabilities of Internet & SaaS and Private Access to cloud-native workloads, enabling enterprises to secure cloud workload communications over any network.
Simplify multi-cloud networking by eliminating complex routing, virtual private networks (VPNs), and firewalls while allowing for flexible forwarding and simple policy management.
Secure workload traffic to the internet and provide seamless connectivity to private applications in other cloud regions or data centers.

cloud-connectors-page.statement: The Cloud Connectors page (Private Access > Private Infrastructure > Cloud Connectors) lists deployed Cloud Connectors with their Name and Cloud Connector Group; by default no filters are applied.

quotes: On the Cloud Connectors page (Private Access > Private Infrastructure > Cloud Connectors)
Filter the Cloud Connector information that appears in the table. By default, no filters are applied.
Name: The name of the Cloud Connector.
Cloud Connector Group: The name of the group that the Cloud Connector is part of.

cloud-connector-groups.statement: Cloud Connector groups are made of individual Cloud Connectors and are used to configure policy rules; they let admins apply policies to a group and upgrade members while maintaining redundancy.

quotes: Cloud Connector groups are comprised of individual Cloud Connectors and are used to configure policy rules in the Zscaler Admin Console.
Apply policies to a group of deployed Cloud Connectors.
Upgrade Cloud Connectors belonging to a group to maintain redundancy while upgrades are being executed.

cloud-connector-groups-page.statement: The Cloud Connector Groups page (Private Access > Private Infrastructure > Cloud Connector Groups) lists deployed groups, with a details drawer per group; by default no filters are applied.

quotes: On the Cloud Connector Groups page (Private Access > Private Infrastructure > Cloud Connector Groups)
View a list of all deployed Cloud Connector groups.
Filter the Cloud Connector group information that appears in the table. By default, no filters are applied.
to open the Cloud Connector Group Details drawer where you can view additional details about the Cloud Connector group.

branch-connector-groups.statement: Branch Connector groups are clusters of Branch Connectors used to configure policy rules; they let admins apply policies to a group and upgrade members while maintaining redundancy, and the page says you can create them in the Zscaler Admin Console using the images shared with your hypervisor.

quotes: Branch Connector groups represent a cluster of individual Branch Connectors used to configure policy rules in the Zscaler Admin Console.
Apply policies to a group of Branch Connectors.
Upgrade Branch Connectors belonging to a group to maintain redundancy while upgrades are being run.
You can create Branch Connector groups in the Zscaler Admin Console using the images shared with your hypervisor.

branch-connector-groups.conditions: Another page selects a New group in a hypervisor configuration template (cloud-connector.sdwan.configuration-templates), so the images are one documented route, not the only one.

branch-connector-groups-page.statement: The Branch Connector Groups page (Private Access > Private Infrastructure > Branch Connector Groups) lists deployed groups, with a details drawer per group; by default no filters are applied.

quotes: On the Branch Connector Groups page (Private Access > Private Infrastructure > Branch Connector Groups)
View a list of all deployed Branch Connector groups.
Filter the Branch Connector group information that appears in the table. By default, no filters are applied.
to open the Branch Connector Group Details drawer

cloud-group-creation.summary: The Private Access page says Cloud Connector groups are created and updated in the Admin Console, while the Cloud Connector overview says they are created automatically on deployment in AWS, Azure or GCP.

quotes: You can create and update Cloud Connector groups in the Zscaler Admin Console.

positions.says: Groups are created and updated in the Admin Console.

quotes: Cloud Connector groups are automatically created when you deploy a Zscaler Cloud Connector in Amazon Web Services (AWS), Microsoft Azure, or Google Cloud Platform (GCP).

positions.says: Groups are created automatically on deployment in AWS, Azure or GCP.

cloud-group-creation.impact: An admin looking for where to create a Cloud Connector group for a cloud deployment may expect a console step the other page says is not needed; the pages do not say whether both apply.

group-limits-and-drawers.title: Limits, group sizes and the contents of the Details drawers for Cloud and Branch Connector groups
group-limits-and-drawers.detail: The Branch and Cloud Connector pages give no limits or group sizes and do not say what the Details drawers show. The Cloud Connector Groups page points to the Step-by-Step Configuration Guide for Zscaler Cloud Connector for creating and updating groups, and the Branch Connector page to image-download pages not in this area.
